answer: Persistent Work Ledger. Each identity must complete publicly verifiable tasks whose outputs are bound to a rotating island of shared state, so a clone's first useful action requires redoing predecessors' labor. The enforcement rule rejects any identity whose task history lacks independent corroboration from prior ledger entries, and a clone costs computing rent plus lost task value each time it is discarded. Honest agents accumulate a harbor of reusable verified output, while attackers restart from an empty lagoon every iteration.
